plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A long-lived herbaceous perennial with large, lush, often fragrant flowers atop sturdy stems with deeply lobed green foliage. Cultivated for thousands of years, it is a staple of cottage gardens and the cut-flower trade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to Central and Eastern Asia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for more than 100 years, and ants are often seen on the buds, feeding on the sugary nectar they secrete.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: A hardy, suckering shrub with fragrant, semi-double to double flowers and golden stamens. It is one of the oldest cultivated roses and a parent of many old garden roses.
plants.location: Native to southern and central Europe and western Asia; grown in gardens throughout the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Rosa gallica 'Officinalis', the Apothecary's Rose, was used medicinally in the Middle Ages and its petals keep their fragrance when dried.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall tree with feathery, fern-like leaves that produces dense clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers. When in bloom, whole streets can be covered in a haze of purple, and fallen petals carpet the ground.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); September to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in warm regions including California, Mexico, Florida, the Mediterranean, and parts of Africa
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, tens of thousands of jacarandas line the streets, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.

plants.name: Leucanthemum vulgare
plants.description: A hardy wildflower with white ray petals around a bright yellow center. It grows in meadows, roadsides, and grasslands, and brings a classic summer look to wild areas.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to late summer (June to August)
plants.location: Native to Europe and temperate Asia; naturalized in North America, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Oxeye daisies are heliotropic in bud, and their flower heads are often used in traditional folk divination games such as 'he loves me, he loves me not'.
